report.summary: Analyzed perfile.py chunk 1/1: defines FileAnalysis dataclass, analyze_file, and analyze_chunk functions with detailed docstrings and comments.
risks: ANALYSIS_VERSION comment | medium | Claim that version '5' is necessary because FileAnalysis now carries type_facts, but version bump logic is fragile if not consistently applied across cache keys. To settle: verify that ANALYSIS_VERSION is included in cache key computation and that all cache reads/writes use the same version constant.

analyze_file for non-python | medium | For non-python languages, type_facts is set to default PyTypeFacts() but comment says 'EXTRACTED UNCONDITIONALLY' yet only Python path extracts type_facts. To settle: confirm that PyTypeFacts() default is acceptable for non-python and that the type-graph layer handles this correctly.

analyze_file docstring | low | Claims 'pure: same inputs -> same outputs, no I/O, no globals', but count_tokens may depend on external tokenizer (tiktoken). To settle: ensure count_tokens is deterministic and has no side effects.
todos: Verify that count_tokens is a pure function with no I/O or external state dependencies.
Ensure that ANALYSIS_VERSION is consistently used in all cache key constructions and that cache invalidation logic is correct.
Confirm that for non-python languages, the default PyTypeFacts() is appropriate and does not cause silent failures in the type-graph layer.

handoff.purpose: Define FileAnalysis dataclass and per-file analysis functions for parallel index building.

symbols.name: ANALYSIS_VERSION
symbols.note: String constant '5' used as part of disk-cache key to invalidate stale entries.

symbols.name: FileAnalysis
symbols.note: Dataclass holding per-file analysis results: rel, lang, n_chars, n_tokens, loc, metrics, units, runs, py_imports, raw_imports, type_facts.

symbols.name: analyze_file
symbols.note: Pure function that analyzes one file given rel, text, spec, and ts_on flag, returning a FileAnalysis instance.

symbols.name: analyze_chunk
symbols.note: Worker entry point for parallel processing: takes a batch job tuple and returns list of (index, FileAnalysis) pairs, preserving original order.

claims.text: Bump whenever the MEANING of any field below changes (new metric, different unit extraction, changed window hashing). It is part of the disk-cache key, so bumping it invalidates every cached entry.
claims.why: The claim that ANALYSIS_VERSION is part of the disk-cache key cannot be verified from this file alone; no cache key construction code is present.

claims.text: "3": added n_tokens. A row cached under "2" has no token count, and an index built from such rows would report a denominator of zero for part of the repo -- i.e. an inflated distillation headline, silently. Bumping makes that unrepresentable.
claims.why: The historical version bumps are described but cannot be verified against the current code; no cache reading logic is present.

claims.text: "4": ``parse.py`` gained the type/field/signature extractor (``PyTypeFacts``). The digest of parse.py is already part of every key, so this bump is belt to that braces -- but the two locks fail differently and only one of them is under our control.
claims.why: Claims about parse.py digest being part of cache key cannot be verified from this file.

claims.text: "5": ``FileAnalysis`` now actually CARRIES them (``type_facts``). "4" rows were written by the generation that had the extractor but not the field, so they have no ``type_facts`` key at all.
claims.why: FileAnalysis dataclass includes type_facts field of type PyTypeFacts. Version '5' is defined.

claims.text: Those rows would decode (``_decode`` reads by subscript, so in fact they raise KeyError and become a miss) -- but relying on a KeyError being raised and swallowed is an accidental lock, not a stated one, and ``_SCHEMA`` was bumped to 2 in the same commit so they are DELETEd on open anyway.
claims.why: No _decode function or _SCHEMA constant is defined in this chunk; the claim refers to code outside this file.

claims.text: This constant is the one a reader greps to answer "which generation of rows is in this cache", and the answer changed.
claims.why: ANALYSIS_VERSION is defined as '5', and the comment explains its purpose.

claims.text: Everything crossing a process boundary is plain data. Nothing here imports ``index`` -- workers must not re-enter the single-flight build lock.
claims.why: The file does not import 'index' (no import statement for it). Data classes and functions use only plain data types.

claims.text: Whole-repo work (import RESOLUTION, the clone passes, churn) deliberately stays in the parent: it needs the full file set, and it is not per-file parallel.
claims.why: No code in this chunk performs whole-repo work; the claim describes intended architecture, not verifiable here.

claims.text: Roughly half the index build is per-file work that depends on nothing but that one file's bytes: unit extraction, health metrics, window-run hashing and raw import extraction.
claims.why: analyze_file function performs unit extraction (extract_units or python_units_imports_and_types), health metrics (file_metrics), window-run hashing (window_runs), and raw import extraction (imports_mod.extract_imports or python_units_imports_and_types).

claims.text: Isolating it here buys two things at once: it can run in a ``ProcessPoolExecutor`` (the work is CPU-bound, so threads are useless under the GIL), and it can be memoized on disk, keyed by content, because the result is a pure function of (rel, spec, text) plus this module's ``ANALYSIS_VERSION``.
claims.why: analyze_file is a pure function (no I/O, no side effects) taking rel, text, spec, ts_on; returns FileAnalysis. The module defines ANALYSIS_VERSION. The function could be run in a process pool.

claims.text: Everything crossing a process boundary is plain data.
claims.why: All data types used (str, int, dict, list, PyTypeFacts) are plain data and picklable.

claims.text: Analyze ONE file. Pure: same inputs -> same outputs, no I/O, no globals.
claims.why: analyze_file function only uses its parameters and calls other pure functions; no I/O or global state is accessed in this function.

claims.text: ONE ast.parse feeds units, imports AND type facts (it used to be two walks of one parse; it is now three walks of the same one).
claims.why: The implementation calls python_units_imports_and_types which is imported from .parse; the claim about number of walks cannot be verified from this file.

claims.text: The units and the import records are produced by the SAME functions as before -- ``python_units_imports_and_types`` adds a third walk, it does not change the first two (invariant I1).
claims.why: Invariant I1 is not defined in this chunk; the behavior of python_units_imports_and_types cannot be verified.

claims.text: Batched rather than one-task-per-file because Windows spawns (not forks) workers, so per-task overhead is real.
claims.why: analyze_chunk processes a batch of files (list of items) in one call, not one file per call.

claims.text: The index tag is what lets the parent restore exact input order regardless of completion order -- ``all_units`` order is load-bearing for the clone passes.
claims.why: analyze_chunk returns list of (index, FileAnalysis) tuples where index is the original position from the input items.

claims.text: EXTRACTED UNCONDITIONALLY, even when the layer is switched off. The gate is in ``index.build_index`` (resolution + publication) and deliberately NOT here: this dataclass rides a CONTENT-KEYED disk cache, so a gate on this side would let a row written with the layer off (empty facts) be served as a HIT to a later build with the layer on.
claims.why: In analyze_file, for non-python languages, type_facts is set to default PyTypeFacts() (empty) and is NOT extracted unconditionally. For python, type_facts is extracted via python_units_imports_and_types. The comment states extraction is unconditional for all languages, but the code only extracts for python. Thus the claim is broken for non-python languages.

claims.text: A frozen dataclass with only tuple fields is hashable and immutable, so it is safe as a PLAIN default (no default_factory) and safe to ship across a process boundary.
claims.why: PyTypeFacts is imported from .parse; its definition (frozen, tuple fields) is not in this chunk. The claim about default_factory is not applicable because the field uses default=PyTypeFacts() which is a mutable default (since PyTypeFacts is a dataclass, not frozen necessarily). The comment says 'frozen dataclass with only tuple fields' but we cannot verify PyTypeFacts is frozen or has only tuple fields.

claims.text: The distill ratio's DENOMINATOR then comes from the same tokenizer as its numerator, instead of a chars/4 guess.
claims.why: No code in this chunk computes distill ratio; the claim refers to usage outside this file.

observations.what: Comment claims type_facts are extracted unconditionally for all languages, but code only extracts for python.
observations.where: FileAnalysis.type_facts field comment vs analyze_file function

observations.what: ANALYSIS_VERSION comments describe historical version bumps and cache key usage, but cache key construction is not in this file.
analyze_file docstring claims 'no I/O' but count_tokens may use external tokenizer (tiktoken) which could involve I/O or non-determinism.
FileAnalysis.type_facts field uses default=PyTypeFacts() which is a mutable default; if PyTypeFacts is not frozen, this could cause shared state.
